name: VEXAS syndrome
aliases: vacuoles E1 enzyme X-linked autoinflammatory somatic syndrome

reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / standard rheumatology references
clinicalPearls: A recently described adult-onset autoinflammatory disease caused by acquired somatic mutations in the UBA1 gene within haematopoietic progenitor cells
The acronym reflects vacuoles in myeloid and erythroid precursors, an E1 (UBA1) enzyme defect, an X-linked pattern, and an autoinflammatory somatic origin
Predominantly affects older men, since the causative UBA1 mutation is X-linked and somatically acquired
Presents with a bridge between rheumatology and haematology, combining severe systemic inflammation with progressive haematological abnormalities
Common inflammatory manifestations include recurrent fevers, neutrophilic dermatosis, chondritis (ear and nose), lung infiltrates, and vasculitis
It overlaps with and can mimic relapsing polychondritis, polyarteritis nodosa, Sweet syndrome, and myelodysplastic syndrome
Characteristic cytoplasmic vacuoles are seen in bone marrow myeloid and erythroid precursor cells, and the diagnosis is confirmed by identifying the somatic UBA1 mutation
Disease is often refractory to conventional immunosuppression; treatment may involve corticosteroids, IL-6 or JAK-directed agents, and allogeneic stem cell transplantation, which can be curative
reference.pathophysiology: Somatic loss-of-function mutations in UBA1, the gene encoding the major E1 ubiquitin-activating enzyme, arise in myeloid progenitor cells and impair the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway. This causes accumulation of misfolded proteins, activation of stress and innate immune signalling, and intense systemic autoinflammation. The mutation also drives clonal haematopoiesis with progressive cytopenias and a strong association with myelodysplastic syndrome, linking the inflammatory and marrow-failure features.
additionalDifferentials: Polyarteritis nodosa and other systemic vasculitides
Sweet syndrome and other neutrophilic dermatoses
Myelodysplastic syndrome and other clonal marrow disorders
additionalInvestigations: Targeted or next-generation sequencing for somatic UBA1 mutations
Bone marrow examination looking for characteristic vacuolated myeloid and erythroid precursors and dysplasia
Full blood count showing macrocytic anaemia, thrombocytopenia, and other cytopenias
Assessment for associated venous thromboembolism and organ-specific inflammation
redFlags: Progressive cytopenias and evolving bone marrow failure or transformation to myelodysplastic syndrome
Vasculitis with organ ischaemia or tissue damage
High rate of venous thromboembolic disease
Refractoriness to standard immunosuppression with cumulative treatment toxicity and high mortality
reference.prognosis: VEXAS carries substantial morbidity and mortality owing to treatment-resistant inflammation, cytopenias, thromboembolism, and progression of the underlying clonal marrow disorder; allogeneic stem cell transplantation offers the only potentially curative option but carries its own significant risks in this typically older population.
pitfalls: Diagnosing seronegative relapsing polychondritis or an idiopathic vasculitis in an older man without testing for UBA1
Overlooking the marrow-failure component and its progression to myelodysplasia
Attributing anaemia solely to chronic inflammation and missing the clonal cause
